headline_decision: The BUG-244 child-refresh recovery is REMOVED, not repaired (HUNT6-A-1). It produced four findings in two days and its recorded residual understated the exposure: a captured request body inside the window is served repeatedly, each serving yielding a full rotating refresh token, so the real exposure is a self-renewing child session until the tablet's next refresh. BUG-244 returns to an accepted, documented open defect and owner action #45 is restored.
note: Lead decisions taken BEFORE the fixers ran. Area file lists are disjoint and their union covers every file the FIXES need, computed from the finders' own fix_touches — lesson L-052 applied at planning time rather than discovered mid-round. Migration numbers are the lead's: 0920/0930 to R6-B, 0940 to R6-E, and 0880 is DELETED by R6-A. scripts/test-minimums.json is the lead's alone.
process_change: Two failure shapes recurred through rounds 4, 5 and 6, and every fixer and checker must test for them BY NAME: (1) a guard that establishes a fact ADJACENT to the one its comment claims — so for each fix, state its premise in one sentence and say what observable fact establishes it; (2) a test that pins the SHAPE of a fix (a source grep, an object literal the test built, a wait on an assertion that cannot fail) rather than the property it exists for — so every test must be shown to go red when the fix is removed.
global_rules: Reproduce first: a test that FAILS for the stated reason before any production change. Paste the failure.
Never weaken a test, an RLS policy, a consent/ZDR gate or a verification step to get a pass.
Approved prices ($39.99 first child + $9.99 each additional, 1-4 paid slots) and the six subjects are settled.
Money is integer cents; time is UTC instants plus IANA zones; domain code takes `now` as input.
JSON into Postgres is ${JSON.stringify(x)}::text::jsonb or tx.json(x), never a bare ::jsonb (L-006).
Mobile token sources come only from apps/mobile/src/lib/app-session.ts (L-007).
Do NOT touch a file outside your list, do not edit anything under docs/ or scripts/test-minimums.json, no repo-wide formatters, no git command that changes state.
State, for each fix, the one-line mutation that turns your test red again.

R6-A-child-refresh-REVERSAL.note: You own the SERVER half of the reversal and the contract. The mobile half belongs to R6-H-mobile, which carries the same decision; do not touch apps/mobile.

lead_decisions.HUNT6-A-1: CONFIRMED, and the lead's decision is NOT another repair: REMOVE the BUG-244 recovery entirely and restore the pre-BUG-244 behaviour, where any presentation of a rotated child refresh token revokes the session. Reasoning, so it is auditable: the recovery's justification was that its exposure was tightly bounded, and this finding shows it is not. A recovery never marks the row it recovered, so the same captured request body is served repeatedly for the whole window, and EACH serving returns a full-lifetime rotating refresh token that then rotates down the ordinary path with no id, no window and no audit row. The two-minute bound limits when the attack can START, not how long it lasts: a captured body buys a self-renewing child session until the real tablet's next refresh, which for a tablet put away is overnight. Against that, the feature only avoids an occasional unpairing a parent can fix by minting a new pairing code. Child privacy is on the never-weaken list, and a logged request body is the realistic capture vector because logs are read later; before BUG-244 such a body was worthless. Four findings in two days against one feature (BUG-248, BUG-249, BUG-286, this) is the feature telling us something. Concretely: delete the recovery branch and RECOVERY_WINDOW_MS from child-auth.ts; delete the audit event it wrote; remove refreshRequestId from the contract; DELETE migration 0880 and its assertions in supabase/tests/hardening_r1_db2.test.ts (the column has never existed in any deployed database, since every Supabase owner action is still open, so an add-then-drop pair would make the schema history describe a feature no running database ever had) and say so in your report; keep and strengthen the tests that pin reuse -> revoke.
lead_decisions.HUNT6-A-2: SUPERSEDED by the A-1 reversal: with no recovery there is no recovery audit row. Delete it with the branch. Do NOT build the ops surface this finding contemplates.
lead_decisions.HUNT6-A-4: CONFIRMED. Fix the stale citation so it names the case that actually pins the rule.

Say plainly in the comment that it is not tracked, and state the exact condition under which it bites. The lead records it in the ledger; you make the comment true.

lead_decisions.HUNT6-D-1: CONFIRMED, and the lead RAISES the four sibling caps rather than leaving four stages promising a retry they cannot afford — the same reasoning already accepted for extraction and grading in BUG-252, and consistency matters more than my comfort with the number. Add the checked helper the finding proposes (fullRaiseCeiling(stage) from the stage's own rates, floor input and output budget), raise coaching, daily_set, thursday_bundle and followup to it, and add a test asserting EVERY stage's cap affords the full raise, so a new stage cannot be added below the line. These caps are guardrails, not spend: holds settle to actual usage, so the raise costs nothing on a call that succeeds and the exposure is a family near their monthly ceiling being asked to wait. REPORT the new per-stage numbers and the new worst-case hold for the lead to record in docs/Cost_Analysis.md; do not edit docs/.

lead_decisions.HUNT6-G-1: CONFIRMED, HIGH, and the most serious finding in this area: the fix gates the session re-read on `unverified`, which only the catch sets, while the real adapter RESOLVES with the refusal — so the re-read never runs and the public page asserts 'This computer is signed out' over a session still readable in that tab. Drop the `unverified &&` guard so both refusal paths re-read, exactly as SignOutControl does; delete the paragraph arguing the in-memory copy can be ignored, because that copy is the fact the sentence is about; navigate with { replace: true }. The three tests that supply a live session and assert the page says it are locking the wrong behaviour IN — rewrite them to assert the opposite, and say in your report which assertions you inverted.

lead_decisions.HUNT6-I-1: CONFIRMED, HIGH. The identity fix rests on a premise about the screens — 'they key their load on the client' — and the Practice planner does not, so publishing fresh state changes nothing there and the next adult keeps the previous family's children, subjects and schedule. Key the planner's loads on the client, AND add the assertion that was missing: a source-level check over every parent screen that its loader invalidates on the client, so the next screen added cannot opt out silently. This is L-037 in its purest form — verified on one surface, assumed for the rest.
lead_decisions.HUNT6-I-2: CONFIRMED. useLoad preserves a ready state across a load-identity change, so the previous adult's rows stay on screen for up to the request timeout. Make the state's owner explicit inside useLoad: when `load` changes identity, drop to loading; a manual reload keeps today's no-flash behaviour because its identity is unchanged.
lead_decisions.HUNT6-I-3: CONFIRMED. Do not tell the family's other adult that THEY asked for the deletion.
lead_decisions.HUNT6-I-4: CONFIRMED. A background lock must not switch adult screen privacy OFF; that is the state the next adult depends on.
lead_decisions.HUNT6-J-1: CONFIRMED, and it is the lead's own hand-written fix from the same day, inert: every step that could leave the device signed in swallows its failure, so the flag means 'no keychain write threw'. Make the sign-out REPORT what it did — have parent-auth return supabase's {error} instead of dropping it, propagate it through the mode helper instead of .catch(() => undefined), and return the outcomes of the two best-effort clears — keeping the 'nothing may stop the sign-out' behaviour and only stopping the hiding. Then replace the source-grep test with one that runs the helper: a test that greps for a ternary passes whatever the helper hides (L-054).
lead_decisions.HUNT6-J-2: CONFIRMED. Keep the screen busy across the whole operation so a second 'Delete my account' cannot be pressed into a live window of up to three network calls, and so the parent gets immediate acknowledgement.
lead_decisions.HUNT6-J-3: CONFIRMED. Do not tell a parent to change a password that no longer exists.
lead_decisions.HUNT6-J-4: CONFIRMED, and it is the same premise error as the cancel fix: a missing local attempt is not proof the server has nothing. Say what is known.
